records.name: Mr. Van Vleck
records.bio: A Boston Society of Natural History annual-report context names Van Vleck with Miss Washburn in arranging and mounting zoological collections and completing Mollusca labelling and cataloguing. The record places this labour beside the Society’s Blaschka processing.
records.open: His full identity and any object-specific work on Blaschka models remain unresolved.

records.name: Giles Tillotson
records.roles: historian · Jaipur museum and exhibition history
records.bio: Tillotson’s study of the Jaipur Exhibition of 1883 supplies institutional context for Thomas Holbein Hendley, the Central Museum and its surviving acquisitions ledger. For this project it helps locate the museum-side archival route needed to close the Jeypore Blaschka order.

records.name: Seiichi Tejima
records.roles: Tokyo Educational Museum actor · catalogue and order contact
records.bio: The Tokyo module identifies Tejima with high confidence behind several corrupted archival name variants. Workshop correspondence and the delivery book connect the Tokyo Educational Museum or Educational Department to catalogues, repeated contact and a completed 1883 Blaschka shipment.
records.open: The exact object list and item-level succession from the 1883 Tokyo shipment remain to be reconstructed.

records.name: Sayaka Kobayashi
records.bio: Kobayashi co-authored a provenance study showing how Tokyo Educational Museum labels can be cross-walked to surviving Tensanbu ledger records. The study concerns a bird collection, so the project uses it as evidence for archival method and record survival rather than as proof for any Blaschka object.
records.open: Application of this ledger method to the Blaschka shipment remains a research task.

records.name: Masaru Kato
records.bio: Kato co-authored the 2020 study demonstrating how Tokyo Educational Museum provenance can be recovered through Tensanbu ledgers. The project treats the result as a methodological and archival-survival anchor, not as direct identification of Blaschka models.
records.open: Application of this ledger method to the Blaschka shipment remains a research task.

records.name: Asami Takada
records.roles: historian of instructional equipment · Tokyo Educational Museum
records.bio: Takada’s study of the Tokyo Educational Museum in the 1880s reconstructs its role in promoting and distributing scientific apparatus and specimens. That institutional history provides the teaching-equipment context for the museum’s documented contact with the Blaschka workshop.

records.name: B.J. Gill
records.bio: Gill co-authored the 2019 reconstruction of the Cheeseman–Ward correspondence and Auckland Museum exchanges. The article establishes the seven surviving Blaschka models, their catalogue numbers, prices, registration numbers and the unrealised plan for a much larger order.

records.name: H.R. Grenfell
records.bio: Grenfell co-authored the 2019 study that reconstructs Auckland Museum’s exchanges with Henry Augustus Ward. Its object-level crosswalk of seven Blaschka models is one of the project’s strongest examples of museum records, dealer correspondence and surviving objects joining cleanly.

records.name: W.M. Blom
records.bio: Blom co-authored the 2019 Auckland Museum study of the Cheeseman–Ward correspondence. The article supplies the archival and registration evidence behind the project’s seven-model Auckland provenance chain and the unfulfilled larger-order proposal.

records.name: Antonio Lazcano Araujo
records.roles: biologist · historian of the Mexico collection
records.bio: Lazcano’s account of emblematic natural-history objects in Mexico identifies surviving Blaschka models and links them to the institutional succession from the old museum at Chopo to later UNAM collections. The project uses his work as a modern collection-history anchor.
